figures.caption: Figure S8. P 2p XPS of uncycled LiPOF-coated NCM particles, cycled composite cathode for both uncoated and coated cells (after 200 cycles at 0.2 C). These data show that P 2p XPS spectra cannot definitively identify the formation of LiPO₃ species, because the coating and any partially oxidized argyrodite that might be formed (if the coating wasn’t ideal) both contain P-Ox species. The P 2p3/2 signal from LiPO3 would appear at a binding energy of 133 eV (the same as reported for Li3PO4; NIST database). These are usually deemed “POx” in the literature and are also where P-Ox signals from oxidized Li6PS5Cl would appear. However, the almost complete lack of oxidized sulfide in the S 2p spectrum (Fig 4b, main text), indicates that the argyrodite is not oxidized, and hence the P-Ox species in the cycled coated cell likely arises from LiPO3.
